description.value:
Politicians make a study of persuasion itself, learning how crowds think, how loyalty is bought, and how a single well-placed word can move armies of people who never even meet. Where other scholars chase facts, these focus on the far messier science of influence.

That mastery follows them past the debate floor and onto the battlefield, where a Politician's presence rallies allies, unravels enemy resolve, and keeps its wielder comfortably out of harm's way. Command, to them, is simply persuasion applied at the point of a blaster.
